description:
A shared, visible Chromium that several AI agents can drive at once.

Hublot runs one visible Chromium browser behind a local broker, and gives each agent its
own tab identified by a label, so several agents can work in the same browser without
interfering with each other. A human can also click and type in that window at any time,
which is what makes it usable for the parts an agent cannot do, such as entering a
password or clearing a two-factor prompt.

The profile is persistent, so cookies and logged-in sessions survive a restart. The
command line covers navigation, clicking, typing, extraction, accessibility snapshots,
screenshots and console or network logs.

It is a command-line tool: there is no window of its own beyond the browser it drives.
0.1.13: on Linux the data folder is now ~/.config/hublot instead of a Windows-style
path (an existing folder is moved, profile included), remote.json, which holds the remote
view token, is written owner-only (0600), and broker.log is capped at 1 MiB with one
previous copy. Windows behaviour is unchanged.
Earlier: Chromium is no longer launched with --disable-web-security (0.1.9) or --no-sandbox
(0.1.12), so the browser's origin isolation and sandbox are back in place. Playwright's
default automation flag is no longer passed to the browser (0.1.10), and clicks now move
the pointer along a path instead of jumping straight to the target (0.1.11).
